encounters.cc: Six-month history of fatigue, constipation, and depression

lines: Six-month history of fatigue, constipation, and depression
She presents to the clinic with a 6-month history of fatigue, constipation, and depression.
Mentions that her mother had a "gland problem" that required surgery.
Her blood pressure is 130/85 mmHg, and her heart rate is 78 bpm.
On physical examination, she appears well, with no obvious abnormalities.
A dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) scan indicates decreased bone mineral density consistent with osteopenia.

encounters.cc: Two-month history of progressive shortness of breath, dry cough, and painful red nodules on shins

lines: Two-month history of progressive shortness of breath, dry cough, and painful red nodules on shins

This 34-year-old African American female with ulcerative colitis and primary hyperparathyroidism diagnosed two months prior presents to the clinic with a 2-month history of progressive shortness of breath, dry cough, and fatigue.
She also reports painful red nodules on her shins that appeared a few weeks ago.
She denies joint pains, eye symptoms, or recent travel.
On physical examination, her vital signs are within normal limits.
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles at the lung bases.
Dermatological examination shows multiple tender, erythematous nodules on the anterior aspects of both lower legs consistent with erythema nodosum.
Chest radiography shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

encounters.cc: Progressive dry cough, mild dyspnea, and fatigue over six months

lines: Progressive dry cough, mild dyspnea, and fatigue over six months
The patient returns for follow-up of sarcoidosis from March 2020.
She presents with a 6-month history of progressive dry cough, mild dyspnea, and fatigue.
She has no history of smoking or recent infections.
On examination, she has mild erythema nodosum on her shins and no wheezing or crackles on lung auscultation.
Laboratory testing shows normal serum phosphate and elevated calcium.
Chest radiograph reveals bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy without focal infiltrates.
A lung biopsy is performed, and histology is shown below.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of dry cough, mild shortness of breath, and occasional fevers

lines: Three-month history of dry cough, mild shortness of breath, and occasional fevers
She denies any significant medical history.
She works as a school teacher and has not traveled recently.
On physical examination, her temperature is 37.8°C (100°F), blood pressure is 120/75 mmHg, pulse is 80 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 18 breaths per minute
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles at the lung bases.
No skin lesions or lymphadenopathy are palpable.
A chest x-ray shows bilateral hilar adenopathy and reticular opacities.

encounters.cc: Three-month history of dry cough, fatigue, and ten-pound unintentional weight loss

lines: Three-month history of dry cough, fatigue, and ten-pound unintentional weight loss

The patient with known sarcoidosis, ulcerative colitis, and primary hyperparathyroidism returns for rheumatology evaluation six months following her last Pulmonology assessment, presenting with a three-month history of dry cough, fatigue, and ten-pound unintentional weight loss.
She denies fever, night sweats, or hemoptysis.
She works as a school teacher and has not traveled recently.
On physical examination, she is afebrile with normal vital signs
Lung auscultation reveals bilateral crackles at the lung bases.
A chest x-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and reticulonodular infiltrates.
A biopsy of a mediastinal lymph node is performed, which shows noncaseating granulomas.

encounters.cc: Persistent fatigue, vague musculoskeletal discomfort, blurry vision, and generalized weakness over six months

lines: Persistent fatigue, vague musculoskeletal discomfort, blurry vision, and generalized weakness over six months
The patient returns for follow-up of her sarcoidosis and primary hyperparathyroidism, previously managed for pulmonary and constitutional symptoms.
She reports generalized weakness, occasional mild headaches, and intermittent blurry vision, particularly when reading at work.
She also endorses mild shortness of breath when carrying groceries upstairs but denies cough, wheezing, fevers, or night sweats.
She has noticed a recent decline in her concentration and productivity.
She does not take any medications
She works as a legal assistant
On review of systems, she mentions experiencing dryness and irritation in her eyes over the past few weeks
Temperature is 36.8°C (98.2°F), blood pressure is 122/80 mmHg, pulse is 78/min, and respiratory rate is 14/min
Neurologic examination shows normal strength and reflexes.
Dermatologic examination is notable for scattered firm, mildly tender, erythematous nodules on the anterior aspects of both lower legs.
Laboratory evaluation reveals normal renal function.
Serum calcium is elevated with suppressed parathyroid hormone levels.
Chest x-ray demonstrates prominent bilateral hilar fullness without lung infiltrates or pleural effusion.

encounters.cc: Three-week history of progressive right-sided facial weakness with persistent dry cough

lines: Three-week history of progressive right-sided facial weakness with persistent dry cough

The patient is a 37-year-old female with established sarcoidosis and primary hyperparathyroidism returning for ongoing evaluation, most recently assessed twelve months prior for constitutional and ocular symptoms.
She also reports a persistent dry cough and occasional shortness of breath over the past two months.
She denies any fever, weight loss, or night sweats.
On physical examination, you note right facial droop with inability to close her right eye or raise her right eyebrow.
Her lung examination reveals bilateral hilar fullness, but no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi.
A chest X-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

encounters.cc: Two-week history of progressively worsening pain and swelling in right knee and left ankle with low-grade fevers

lines: Two-week history of progressively worsening pain and swelling in right knee and left ankle with low-grade fevers
The patient with sarcoidosis, ulcerative colitis, hyperparathyroidism, and prior facial weakness presents.
She denies recent trauma to the affected joints but reports low-grade fevers and a rash on her lower legs.
Her ulcerative colitis has been well-controlled on mesalamine.
Physical examination reveals a warm, swollen right knee with limited range of motion due to pain, and a similarly affected left ankle.
There is no evidence of joint erosion or deformity.
A pustular rash is noted on her lower extremities.
Radiographs of the affected joints show soft tissue swelling without joint space narrowing, erosions, or osteopenia.
